Collaborator

Dev Engineer Review

  • Adds in-tree Staircase routing with off, auto, and require modes controlled by TRTLLM_STAIRCASE.
  • Adds SM103 targets for GPT-OSS 120B TP1 and DeepSeek-R1-0528 NVFP4 DEP4.
  • Adds target-specific modeling, weight loading, YAML configurations, operator wrappers, and catalog contracts.
  • Adds extensive operator documentation and packaging entries.
  • Main risks are CUDA-only execution, strict checkpoint and topology matching, custom-operator availability, and complex weight relayout and quantization paths.
  • Verify that AutoModelForCausalLM preserves existing behavior when routing is disabled or unmatched.
  • Verify that require fails with actionable diagnostics and that lazy target imports do not create import-time regressions.
  • Review memory settings, MTP configurations, and TRTLLM_CAN_USE_DEEP_EP=0 requirements for consistency across launch environments.

QA Engineer Review

  • Adds unit coverage for activation, normalization, attention, GEMM, MoE, quantization, communication, routing, and target-artifact contracts.
  • Adds multi-rank CUDA/MPI tests for allgather and reducescatter, including CUDA Graph, stream, validation, call-order, and wedge behavior.
  • Adds integration accuracy tests for GPT-OSS 120B and DeepSeek-R1, including identity, MTP3 acceptance, GSM8K accuracy, and default routing behavior.
  • Adds CI test-list entries in l0_gb300.yml and l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml for operator, collective, accuracy, and default-behavior coverage.
  • Coverage is sufficient for the documented CUDA and SM103 scope, but requires follow-up on unsupported architectures, non-CUDA environments, package-data installation, and full checkpoint loading.

Per-File QA Perspective

  • tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_auto.py: Verify disabled, automatic, required, matched, and unmatched Staircase resolution paths.
  • tensorrt_llm/_torch/staircase/_router_index.py, __init__.py, explain.py, and routing modules: Verify environment parsing, diagnostics, lazy imports, target identity, and unsupported-topology behavior.
  • Staircase catalog Python files: Verify wrapper signatures, tensor validation, custom-op registration, mutation contracts, dtype behavior, and unsupported-input errors.
  • Staircase catalog Markdown and index.yaml files: Verify documented signatures, certified configurations, limits, and implementation paths match the wrappers and tests.
  • Staircase target modeling.py and weights.py files: Verify model construction, operator availability checks, weight coverage, tensor layouts, dtype handling, and post-load views against real checkpoints.
  • Target YAML files: Verify topology, MTP settings, memory limits, environment requirements, and launch-time defaults.
  • setup.py: Verify all Staircase Markdown and YAML files are included in source and wheel distributions.
  • tests/unittest/_torch/staircase/**: Covers operator contracts, numerical behavior, edge cases, validation, routing, and artifact consistency. These tests are listed through the Staircase entries in tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300.yml where applicable.
  • tests/unittest/_torch/staircase/comm/**: Covers launcher-driven four-rank collective behavior. The matrix entry points are listed in tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml.
  • tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_staircase.py: Covers GPT-OSS and DeepSeek accuracy, identity, MTP acceptance, and default routing. Its acceptance tests are listed in tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml.
  • tests/integration/defs/accuracy/references/*.yaml: Provides accuracy and acceptance-length thresholds used by the integration tests. Verify reference provenance and threshold updates before changing certified results.
  • tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300.yml: Adds single-GPU Staircase operator and model coverage.
  • tests/integration/test_lists/test-db/l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml: Adds ordered collective coverage and DeepSeek accuracy acceptance coverage.

tensorrt_llm/_torch/staircase/catalog/comm/_rank_job.py-76-82 (1)

76-82: 🩺 Stability & Availability | 🟡 Minor | ⚡ Quick win

A timeout here kills the launcher only, not the mpirun ranks.

subprocess.run(timeout=...) kills the direct child. The child is the launcher, and the launcher puts mpirun in a separate session (start_new_session=True in allgather_test.py line 974). When this timeout fires, the wedged ranks are not in the killed process group. They can keep running and hold the GPUs for the rest of the pytest session.

This path is reached only when the entry's own deadline also fails to fire, so it is a backstop. Start the launcher in its own session and kill the group on timeout.

🛡️ Proposed fix to kill the launcher's whole group 
-    completed = subprocess.run(
-        [sys.executable, str(launcher)],
-        env=env,
-        capture_output=True,
-        text=True,
-        timeout=timeout,
-    )
-    if completed.returncode != 0:
+    process = subprocess.Popen(
+        [sys.executable, str(launcher)],
+        env=env,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+        text=True,
+        start_new_session=True,
+    )
+    try:
+        stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
+        stdout, stderr = process.communicate()
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{launcher.name} did not finish in {timeout}s (wedged)"
+        ) from None
+    if process.returncode != 0:
         raise AssertionError(
-            f"{launcher.name} exited {completed.returncode}\n"
-            f"--- stdout ---\n{completed.stdout}\n"
-            f"--- stderr ---\n{completed.stderr}"
+            f"{launcher.name} exited {process.returncode}\n"
+            f"--- stdout ---\n{stdout}\n"
+            f"--- stderr ---\n{stderr}"
         )

Add import signal next to the existing imports.

13-13: 📐 Maintainability & Code Quality | 🔵 Trivial | ⚡ Quick win

Restore allow_tf32 instead of mutating it at import time. Both modules set torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False at module scope and never restore it. pytest imports every selected module into one worker process, so this setting leaks into every module collected afterwards, and the leak depends on collection order. A later test that relies on the TF32 default then runs with a different matmul backend than it expects.

test_staircase_cublas_mm.py Lines 14-36 already solves this correctly with the _true_fp32_matmul context manager, which saves and restores both allow_tf32 and fp32_precision. Reuse that pattern, or scope the change with an autouse fixture that restores the previous value.

46-46: 📐 Maintainability & Code Quality | 🔵 Trivial | ⚡ Quick win

Gate the CUDA requirement with a skip marker, not a module-level assert. Every new op test module asserts torch.cuda.is_available() at import time. On a host without a visible GPU that assert fires during collection, so pytest reports a collection error for the whole module instead of a skip. A collection error cannot be distinguished from a real defect, and it aborts every test in the file at once. Replace the assert with pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason=...) so the requirement is a precise capability gate.

Use explicit exceptions for public contract validation.

Python removes these assertions under -O or -OO. A wrongly shaped out can then reach torch.ops.trtllm.bmm_out, which silently resizes it and violates the exact-shape, caller-provided-buffer contract. Replace all three assertions with explicit ValueError checks.

Reject every dtype outside the certified arithmetic-sum set.

The wrapper rejects only torch.float8_e4m3fn. ReducescatterOp::run_list opens the NCCL group before TorchUtils::dataType(). Thus, torch.float64 and unsupported float8 formats throw before ncclGroupEnd(), and later collectives can return invalid data. torch.bool maps to ncclInt8 with ncclSum, so its underlying bytes are summed and the boolean result behaves like OR. torch.quint4x2 also reaches the native operation although getDtypeMap() has no kINT4 entry.

Use an allowlist of the dtypes certified by reducescatter.md, and add wrapper tests for torch.float64, every unsupported float8 format, torch.bool, and torch.quint4x2.

Do not use assert for required input validation.

When Python runs with -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE, it removes the assertion. A multi-element global_scale can then reach torch.ops.trtllm.fp4_quantize; the native implementation passes its pointer to the kernel, which reads element 0 for every row. This can produce incorrectly quantized output.

Raise ValueError explicitly and add a regression test that passes a two-element global_scale and asserts the exception.

Comment on lines +12 to +21
def _check(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor, out: torch.Tensor) -> None:
ref = torch.bmm(a.float(), b.float()).to(out.dtype)
bmm_out(a, b, out)
# rtol: torch.testing defaults per output dtype. atol: kernel and reference
# both accumulate in fp32 but in different summation orders; for K <= 1024
# unit-variance inputs the order-dependent absolute noise is up to
# ~K * 2^-24 ~= 6e-5, which dominates on near-zero outputs produced by
# cancellation, so atol=1e-3 instead of the ~1e-5 defaults.
rtol = {torch.bfloat16: 1.6e-2, torch.float16: 1e-3, torch.float32: 1.3e-6}
torch.testing.assert_close(out, ref, rtol=rtol[out.dtype], atol=1e-3)

[TRTLLM-16304][feat] In-tree implementation of staircase
c3f526f 
Staircase is one self-contained forward per (checkpoint, GPU architecture,
parallel topology) triple, assembled only from a catalog of certified ops and
trusted through accuracy gates rather than shared abstractions. Where
_torch/models/modeling_deepseekv3.py is one class serving every checkpoint and
topology, _torch/staircase/models/deepseek_v3/ is one flat codebase per target.
The two live side by side and the contrast is the point.

Entry is an environment variable:

    TRTLLM_STAIRCASE=require

"off" -- unset, the default -- is byte-for-byte today's behaviour: the resolver
returns immediately and nothing in the package is imported. "auto" uses a
target when one matches. "require" raises instead of falling back, because a
silent fallback would attribute the built-in implementation's numbers to
staircase. An unrecognised value raises rather than reading as "off", for the
same reason.

A variable rather than an LLM-API field, so that nothing outside this package
carries the concept and the only upstream change staircase needs is the
resolver hook itself. It has to be exported before the ranks start, not merely
before LLM(...): worker ranks receive the environment as it stood when MPI
initialized, so a value set later reaches the driver and not them -- and a
driver resolving a staircase target while its workers resolve the built-in is
exactly the silent split "require" exists to prevent.

Routing follows an existing upstream pattern. Targets are keyed by a synthetic
architecture name no checkpoint declares, reached through a rewrite in
AutoModelForCausalLM._resolve_class -- the same shape as
MTPDraftModelForCausalLM. A small table maps architectures[0] to a routing
module; that module owns one forward-reading decision tree, so reading a single
file tells you where any configuration lands, and explain.py replays the same
tree to say why. The package sits beside _torch/models/ rather than inside it
so its registrations count as external and win their slot, and so the zoo's
non-recursive staleness scan is not broken. The upstream footprint is
seventeen lines: the hook in modeling_auto.py, and two package_data patterns
in setup.py for the TARGET.md and configs/ that a gate command reads from the
installed tree.

This batch brings two targets and the 30 catalog entries they call (19 trtllm
ops with contract, wrapper and GPU test; 11 thin torch mirrors).

Validated on GB300 (sm_103), trtllm 1.3.0rc26:

  catalog                          19/19 entries, 312 cells, plus both 4-rank
                                   collective matrices
  gpt-oss-120b / tp1               boot 10/10; gsm8k 90.6748 vs threshold
                                   85.5989
  r1-0528-nvfp4 / dep4             boot 10/10; gsm8k 95.0720 vs threshold
                                   89.9962
  r1 configs/mtp3.yaml             boot 10/10; paired gsm8k delta -0.3791
                                   against a |delta| < 1.2 criterion;
                                   acceptance_length 3.3514 against stock's
                                   3.2752

Every checkpoint digest was verified against the target's own record, so the
new gate records and the pre-move sm_100 ones were measured on byte-identical
weights.

Four differences surfaced while re-certifying the catalog on sm_103, none
resolved by widening a tolerance:

  - Three ops' schemas changed between rc21 and rc26 (renamed and added
    parameters). The wrappers now mirror their schemas argument for argument.
  - The MoE FC1 epilogue's MXFP8 block scale is floor(log2(amax))-8 on sm_100
    and ceil(log2(amax/448)) on sm_103, bit-exactly. The reference is now
    architecture-keyed and each arch refutes the other's recipe.
  - torch 2.12 defaults fp32 matmul to TF32, so cublas_mm's *reference* was the
    imprecise side; the op is bit-identical to a TF32-disabled product.
  - The MLA append op now accepts NVFP4 latent pools as well as fp8.

Measured statements in the migrated contracts are left exactly as written.
They are true records of what was observed on sm_100; rewriting them would
manufacture GB300 evidence that does not exist. Receipts are per architecture.

[TRTLLM-16304][test] Wire the staircase catalog tests into the unit t…
031a472 
…est suite

The catalog's GPU tests were living beside their contracts and wrappers inside
tensorrt_llm/_torch/staircase/catalog/, which is where the upstreaming plan put
them -- but nothing collects tests from the package. The two in-tree precedents
for a test inside tensorrt_llm/ (cute_dsl_kernels/test_argmax.py,
kv_cache_manager_v2/rawref/test_rawref.py) are on no list either. So they move
to tests/unittest/_torch/staircase/, which is the tree CI collects from.

Named test_staircase_<entry>.py rather than test_<entry>.py for two reasons.
Three would otherwise collide with an upstream test of the same basename, and
under pytest's default import mode a duplicate basename is an import error.
More importantly they are not duplicates of those tests: upstream covers the
modules that wrap these ops, these cover the op itself cell by cell -- the
strategy x operation matrix, which strategies are bitwise identical, which
combinations are silently wrong rather than loud. Distinct names keep review
from reading one as a copy of the other.

The two collective entries keep their rank bodies in catalog/comm/. The
launcher re-execs them as `python -m` and the ranks need that package context
for their relative imports; only the collected shells moved.

Test list entries, and why they are on these two lists:

  l0_gb300.yml              unittest/_torch/staircase, comm excluded
  l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml   unittest/_torch/staircase/comm

The catalog's certification is per GPU architecture -- receipts are keyed by
sm -- and these are the sm_103 lists. The collectives are on the 4-GPU list
because they are certified at world size 4, which is dep4's topology.

An entry now spans two trees, so the receipt rule gains a second directory to
look in: a receipt is valid only if it post-dates the last write to every file
of the entry, contract and wrapper and test alike. index.yaml and the README
say so.

Verified on GB300 (sm_103), run from tests/ with the exact path strings the
lists carry: 343 passed for the single-GPU entry, 2 passed for the collective
entry (each spawning its own 4-rank job).

[TRTLLM-16304][test] Add the staircase whole-model gates to the accur…
e6f0f13 
…acy suite

The op-level entries certify the vocabulary; these certify the assemblies that
call it. A separate file rather than entries in test_llm_api_pytorch.py, for
the same reason the targets are separate codebases: reading them beside the
built-in model's tests would invite treating one as a variant of the other.

  l0_gb300.yml               TestStaircaseGptOss120bSm103Tp1::test_gsm8k
                             test_staircase_off_is_the_default
  l0_gb300_multi_gpus.yml    TestStaircaseDeepseekR10528Nvfp4Sm103Dep4::
                               test_gsm8k
                               test_gsm8k_identity_vs_mtp3
                               test_mtp3_acceptance[staircase]
                               test_mtp3_acceptance[stock]

Two of these are shaped unlike an ordinary accuracy test, for reasons worth
stating.

**identity vs mtp3 is one test, not two.** Both measurements are taken in a
single case on purpose. The same identity forward measured 94.7688 and 95.0720
on consecutive days -- 0.30 apart on bit-identical code -- so a delta against a
score recorded in an earlier session carries that session's variance into the
judgement. Paired, the variance is common to both and cancels. Three runs here:
+0.3412, +0.9477, +0.3033, against a |delta| < 1.2 criterion.

**Acceptance is two independent cases sharing one anchor.** Rejection sampling
makes a miscomputed draft path slower rather than wrong, so smoke and accuracy
are both blind to it and acceptance length is the only detector. The two legs
are read against the same recorded minimum, which is what makes the pair
informative: staircase failing while stock passes means the draft path
regressed; both failing means the anchor is stale and should be re-derived
rather than the target blamed. The anchor is populated from the stock leg --
taking it from the target's own number would make the gate self-referential,
the same rule the accuracy anchors follow.

min_al is hand-set to 2.5 rather than the automatic 95% of the reference.
Measured over three runs each on GB300: stock 3.020/2.998/3.009/3.014,
staircase 2.921/2.938/2.933. Each side is stable to ~0.7% and the ranges do not
overlap, so staircase sits about 2.6% under stock consistently. The automatic
floor of 2.869 would have left the staircase leg 1.8% of headroom against a
0.7% spread -- a flaky test rather than a gate. 2.5 is a collapse tripwire, the
role the TestKimiK3DSpark entry already documents.

Also needed:

  - a gsm8k.yaml reference for R1-0528 NVFP4 + FP8 KV + MTP. Same accuracy as
    the non-MTP entry: MTP is distribution-preserving, so it must not move the
    score, which is what the paired test asserts directly.
  - scores_filter bound to exact_match,flexible-extract. Unset, the evaluator
    averages the filters, and for gpt-oss that means the mean of ~90 flexible
    and ~25 strict -- 56.1, which reads as catastrophic failure of a model
    answering correctly.
  - an output budget of 8192 for gpt-oss. The stock 256 truncates this
    reasoning model mid-chain-of-thought, before it reaches an answer.

Verified on GB300 (sm_103), run from tests/ with the list path strings:
1-GPU 2 passed (gsm8k 89.083 against the 90.300 reference), 4-GPU 4 passed
(acceptance staircase 2.933 / stock 3.014).

[TRTLLM-16304][test] Keep the staircase collectives off xdist, drop a…
8d70c24 
… redundant gate

Two follow-ups on the staircase CI wiring.

**The collective entries are marked no_xdist.** Each case starts its own
4-rank mpirun over every visible device, so several xdist workers would fight
for the same GPUs. The runner does retry failures serially, so this would
likely still go green -- but only after a confusing parallel failure. The
marker is what the other collective entry in this repo
(_torch/thop/serial/test_moe_alltoall.py) uses for the same reason.

Note on the parallel config: agg_unit_mem_df.csv gets no entries here. Its
header says it is generated from execution results by the infra team and not
manually edited, and it currently carries no GB300 rows at all, so every
GB300 unittest entry already falls back to serial with a warning. That is a
pre-existing condition for that list rather than something these entries
introduce, and hand-writing rows would contradict the file's stated policy.

**The standalone R1 identity gsm8k case is gone.** test_gsm8k_identity_vs_mtp3
evaluates the identity config as its first leg, and task.evaluate asserts
accuracy against the registered reference on the way past, so the separate
case gated nothing new while costing an engine boot of a 61-layer model on 4
ranks. Both the docstring and a comment where the case used to be now say that
